A row's words are the DISTINCT tokens of its beverage_house_key. The row whose key equals the name's key wins (exact); else the row with the most words among those whose every word the name holds (contains); rows level at the top tie, the name joins none of them, and each tied row counts the name's lines in tied_lines; a name that joins no row keeps its own key (a row only when the queue ever held it). The join is an equi-join on the word (name_word to book_word), never every name against every row. The verify holds while, in the newest migration that defines public.house_beverage_ledger (comments stripped): book is the union of menu_agg, inv_agg, ord_agg and quo_agg; book_word takes SELECT DISTINCT words and counts them per key as n; reach joins name_word to book_word ON the word, grouped by (name, row), HAVING count(*) = min(bw.n); pick labels exact first, then a count over (name_k, n) above 1 as tie, and ranks exact first then n descending; pour_on joins the winner only (rnk = 1 AND how <> 'tie', exactly once) and keeps an unjoined name on its own key through NOT EXISTS of such a winner; tie_agg joins rnk = 1 AND how = 'tie'; pour_agg groups FROM pour_on BY k; and the row returns coalesce(tz.lines, 0) AS tied_lines. Pinned by the migration's SQL test (a_till_name_with_a_serve_size_joins_its_row, S1-S5 and S7).
